key_insight: Al-Ghasali models closed Islamic jurisprudential chapters as deterministic finite-state automata, using constrained LLM generation to verbalize rather than decide rulings.
engineering_relevance: The framework separates deterministic decision logic from probabilistic language generation, targeting constant-time verdict lookup after offline compilation.
method: Compile finite propositional Horn-rule theories into deterministic automata.
Encode temporal requirements as explicit states and compose subchapter automata.
Constrain LLM output with execution-derived right-linear grammars, a bounded neutral lexicon, and valence locking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports formal proofs of computational and output-safety properties, but no empirical datasets, benchmarks, or user evaluations.
watch_item: The claimed guarantees depend on correct rule formalization and constraint enforcement; compilation cost and state-space growth remain practical concerns.
paper_title: Al-Ghasali: A Computational Framework for Simulating Islamic Jurisprudential Rulings via Finite State Automata and Large Language Models
